def factor_volatility_regime_blend(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    vol = ret.rolling(20).std()
    vol_median = vol.rolling(40).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    weight = (vol / vol_median).clip(0, 1)
    weight = weight.fillna(0.5)
    mean_rev = -ret.shift(1)
    momentum = df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].shift(20) - 1
    raw = (1 - weight) * mean_rev + weight * momentum
    raw = raw.rolling(5).mean()
    df_copy["factor_volatility_regime_blend"] = raw
    return df_copy["factor_volatility_regime_blend"]
formula: weight = clip(vol / vol_median, 0, 1); factor = (1-weight)*(-1d_ret) + weight*(20d_ret); smoothed
rationale: Replaces the binary volatility regime switch with a continuous blend of short-term reversal and long-term momentum, weighted by relative volatility. When volatility is very low, the factor leans on mean-reversion; when volatility is very high, it leans on momentum; in between, it smoothly combines both signals. This reduces abrupt transition noise and preserves the core economic intuition of regime-dependent market behavior.
